title: Slowly, by God's Hand Unfurled
description: Slowly, by God's Hand Unfurled in Tonic Solfa to INNOCENTS, doh is D: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 4 verses and a piano.
about: William Henry Furness wrote these words. They were printed in A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion, compiled by Samuel Longfellow and Samuel Johnson (Boston, 1848), as hymn 371, “The Light of Stars”. The compilers changed some of the words, and this is their version.
The book printed the words without tunes, marked Sevens (7.7.7.7) (7.7.7.7), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to INNOCENTS; any other Sevens (7.7.7.7) tune fits them as well.
underlay: Slow-ly, by God's hand un-furled, Down a-round the wea-ry world Falls the dark-ness; O, how still Is the work-ing of His will!

lines: Falls the darkness; O, how still
Is the working of His will!
Living stars to view be brought
In the boundless realms of thought;
Let them break upon my sight;
Let them shine serene and still,
And with light my being fill.

source: A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion (1848)
licence: Public domain: William Henry Furness died in 1896.
credits: Words by William Henry Furness (1802–1896), public domain, as printed in A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion (1848); set to INNOCENTS by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
